title: Optimal Transport under Group Fairness Constraints
claim: Unconstrained matching concentrates mass within matching groups; specifying group-level targets and two relaxations yields plans that follow those targets.
layout: 3 panels left-to-right, gray dividers, heatmap-to-targets-to-method formulas
description: Three panels separated by gray vertical lines. Left: two dashed blobs holding blue (μ) and red (η) distribution clouds labeled by group attributes S and W, beside a 'Vanilla OT Map' heatmap in red shades. The heatmap is a block matrix with S rows and W columns, and mass concentrates on the diagonal blocks where the groups match. Center: two 2x2 grids titled 'Fairness Targets'. Cells are shaded red to show desired group-pair matching probabilities, and some cells are white to mean no matches. Captions read 'No matches between groups S=W' and 'S=W=0'. Right: 'Penalized OT' shows the objective with entropic regularization and a highlighted red penalty term λL_F(π). Below it, 'Cost Learning' shows blobs passing through a learned transformation box into rearranged points. The eye goes first to the red heatmap and the 2x2 target grids.
caption: Illustration of optimal transport under group fairness constraints. Left: Due to the correlation between group attributes (S and W) and features, vanilla optimal transport produces transport plans that concentrate most of the mass between matching groups. Center: Our novel notion of fairness is based on fairness targets, defined as the desired group-level matching probabilities specified by a central planner. Right: We propose two approaches for solving this problem: a fairness-penalized optimal transport method, and a cost-learning approach that transforms the input space so that the resulting optimal transport plan aligns as closely as possible with the fairness targets.
abstract: Ensuring fairness in matching algorithms is a key challenge in allocating scarce resources and positions. Focusing on Optimal Transport (OT), we introduce a novel notion of group fairness requiring that the probability of matching two individuals from any two given groups in the OT plan satisfies a predefined target. We first propose a modified Sinkhorn algorithm to compute perfectly fair transport plans efficiently. Since exact fairness can significantly degrade matching quality in practice, we then develop two relaxation strategies. The first one involves solving a penalized OT problem, for which we derive novel finite-sample complexity guarantees. Our second strategy leverages bilevel optimization to learn a ground cost that induces a fair OT solution, and we establish a bound on the deviation of fairness when matching unseen data. Finally, we present empirical results illustrating the performance of our approaches and the trade-off between fairness and transport cost.
